newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD says against any cuts to pensions.
newsitem.headline: German SPD says against any cuts to pensions.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Sunday said they were against any cuts to the country's generous state pensions, which the government wants to overhaul along with the tax system.

Rudolf Dressler, the head of the SPD pension commission, said it was very unlikely that the party would be able to agree with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition on a joint approach to pension reform.
But Dressler said in order to show the willingness of the SDP to negotiate on the issue the party would still take part in discussions with the ruling coalition on Tuesday.
He said if these talks failed Germany's citizens would have to decide at next year's general elections whether they wanted a structural reform of the pensions system or lasting cuts.
The SPD pension commission also said it was against the raising of the pensionable age.

"This would only be a topic (for discussion) when life expectancy had noticeably increased for decades," said Dressler, speaking after the commission ended a three day meeting here in this town near Bonn.

Pension experts in Kohl's ruling coalition's agreed last month on a plan to reform the pensions system over the next 20 years, after twice putting off a decision on the subject, but they did not give details of what they had decided.

Labour Minister Norbert Bluem, who has championed an overhaul, has sought to cut pension contributions to below 20 percent of wages, from the current 20.3 percent level. He also wanted to lower pension benefits to 64 percent of average net wages after 45 years of work -- down from 70 percent today.
